# iliad-066 — new renderings (Iliad 11.221–327)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἐριβώλακι μητέρι μήλων (Θρῄκῃ, 11.222) | "rich-soiled, mother of sheep" | "of the rich soil, the mother of flocks" | "fertile", "nurse of flocks" (kept for βωτιάνειρα "nurse of men"), "mother of sheep and goats" (μῆλα is small livestock, and the note says so); follows ἐριβῶλαξ "rich-soiled" (1.155, 6.315) |
| μητροπάτωρ (11.224) | "his mother’s father" | "his mother’s father" | "maternal grandfather", "grandfather" (loses the compound’s plain parts μήτηρ + πατήρ) |
| χάλκεον ὕπνον κοιμήσατο (11.241) | "slept a bronze sleep" | "slept a bronze sleep" (+ note: death by the bronze weapon) | "slept the sleep of death", "sank into a brazen slumber", "died" (each explains the image away) |
| μνηστῆς ἀλόχου … κουριδίης (11.242–243; the Greek says "wedded" twice) | "his wedded wife … the wedded one" | "his wedded wife … his wedded wife" | "betrothed", "bride", "lawful wife", "the wife of his youth" (avoided by the table’s μνηστῇ ἀλόχῳ and κουριδίην ἄλοχον); both words keep "wedded", as the table has them singly, and the note says the Greek repeats |
| ἧς οὔ τι χάριν ἴδε (11.243) | "of whom no delight he saw" | "of whom he had no joy" | "no thanks", "no gratitude", "no return" (χάρις covers delight, favour and thanks, and the note says so) |
| ἀνεμοτρεφὲς ἔγχος (11.256) | "wind-nurtured spear" | "wind-nurtured spear" (+ note: meaning not known) | "wind-swift", "wind-borne", "grown in the wind" (each picks a sense); ἄνεμος "wind" + τρέφω "nourish" |
| στῆ δ’ εὐρὰξ (11.251) | "stood sideways" | "took his stand to one side" (+ note: rare word, usual gloss) | "from behind", "aslant", "broadside"; εὐρά́ξ keeps the usual "sideways" |
| ἀκωκή (δουρὸς ἀκωκή, 11.253) | "tip" | "tip" | "point" (kept for αἰχμή, which this part has at 11.237), "edge", "head"; departs from the Odyssey, which ships "point" for δουρὸς ἀκωκή (odyssey-096), because "point" is the house word for αἰχμή and this part has both words, 11.237 and 11.253, in one passage |
| κασίγνητον καὶ ὄπατρον (11.257) | "his brother and born of the same father" | "his brother … born of the same father" | "half-brother", "full brother" (both decide what the Greek leaves open), "brother by the same father"; ὄπατρος is ὁ- "together" + πατήρ |
| πρεσβυγενής (11.249) | "eldest-born" | "the eldest son" | "elder", "first-born" (reserved for πρωτόγονος), "venerable" |
| ἐπεπωλεῖτο στίχας ἀνδρῶν (τῶν ἄλλων, 11.264) | "was going about the ranks of the other men" | "ranged along the ranks of the other men" | follows the table’s ἐπεπωλεῖτο στίχας ἀνδρῶν (4.231); τῶν ἄλλων "of the other men" added |
| χερμαδίοισι (μεγάλοισί τε χερμαδίοισιν, 11.265) | "great stones" | "great stones" | "boulders", "rocks", "slingstones"; χερμάδιον is a stone that fills the hand, and the note says so |
| ἀνήνοθεν (11.266, old perfect, present sense) | "welled up" | "welled" | "gushed", "oozed", "sprang"; the root is not certain |
| ὀξεῖαι ὀδύναι δῦνον μένος (11.268 = 11.272) | "sharp pains entered the might" | "sharp pains entered the might" | "pangs" (kept for ὠδῖνες), "bitter" (kept for πικρός), "sank into his strength"; the same wording at both places |
| μογοστόκοι Εἰλείθυιαι (11.270) | "the travail-bringing Eileithyiae" | "the Eileithyiae … the goddesses of the travail of birth" | "the birth-goddesses" alone, "the goddesses of childbirth" (drops μόγος "toil"), "Eileithyiai", "Eilithyias"; μογοστόκος is μόγος "toil, travail" + τόκος "birth" |
| πικρὰς ὠδῖνας (11.271) | "bitter pangs" | "the bitter pangs" | "sharp" (kept for ὀξύς), "birth-pains", "throes"; ὠδίς "pang of labour" |
| βέλος ὀξὺ δριμύ (11.269–270) | "a sharp shaft … a keen one" | "a sharp, keen shaft" | "bitter" (kept for πικρός), "piercing", "stinging"; βέλος "shaft" per the table, δριμύς "keen" |
| ἤχθετο γὰρ κῆρ (11.274) | "for he was distressed in heart" | "for he was distressed at heart" | "pained", "vexed", "angry"; "distressed" is the table’s ἀχθομένη, and κῆρ is "heart" in the accusative of respect, as in χωόμενος κῆρ "incensed at heart" |
| ἔδωκε (μέγ’ εὖχος ἔδωκε Ζεὺς Κρονίδης, 11.288–289) | "a great boast has given Zeus, the son-of-Cronus" | "Zeus, the son of Cronus, has given me a great triumph" | "great cause to boast" (the table’s 5.285 wording), "glory" (reserved for κῦδος); follows the table’s εὖχος … δώῃ (7.81) and δῶκεν … εὖχος (7.154): "boast" in `l`, "triumph" in `i` |
| οἴχετ’ ἀνὴρ ὤριστος (11.288) | "He is gone, the man, the best" | "The best man has gone" | "the best of men", "our best foe" (adds), "is dead" (οἴχομαι is only "gone"); ὤριστος = ὁ ἄριστος |
| ἀργιόδοντας κύνας (11.292) | "white-toothed dogs" | "white-toothed dogs" | "white-fanged", "bright-toothed"; follows the table’s ἀργιόδοντας ὕας "white-toothed pigs" (8.60) |
| ἀγροτέρῳ συῒ καπρίῳ (11.293) | "a wild swine, a boar" | "a wild boar" | "a field boar", "a wild pig and boar" (two nouns collapsed in `i`, both kept in `l`), "a savage boar" |
| Ἕκτωρ Πριαμίδης βροτολοιγῷ ἶσος Ἄρηϊ (11.295) | "Hector, Priam’s-son, equal to mortal-ruining Ares" | "Hector, son of Priam, the equal of Ares, the ruin of mortals" | "man-slaying Ares", "Ares the bane of men", "like Ares"; Πριαμίδης "Priam’s-son" (2.817), βροτολοιγὸς Ἄρης "mortal-ruining Ares" / "Ares, the ruin of mortals" (8.115), ἶσος "equal to" as in ἀτάλαντος Ἄρηϊ "the equal of Ares" |
| μέγα φρονέων (11.296; again μέγα φρονέοντε, 11.325) | "greatly thinking" | "full of proud thoughts" | "exulting", "puffed up", "high-minded", "confident" (each picks a feeling); μέγα "greatly" + φρονέω "think", as in the table’s φίλα φρονέων "thinking kindly" |
| ὑπεραέϊ ἀέλλῃ (11.297) | "a blast blowing from above" | "a storm blowing down from above" (+ note: sense of ὑπερ- not certain) | "a gale from on high", "a howling blast", "a storm-blast"; ἄελλα is "blast" in `l` and "storm" in `i` (table), and ὑπεραής is ὑπέρ "over" + ἄημι "blow" |
| ἀργεστᾶο Νότοιο (11.306) | "of the bright South Wind" | "of the bright South Wind" (+ note: meaning not known) | "clear-skied", "white-clearing", "cloud-clearing", "Argestes" (each picks a sense or makes it a name) |
| τρόφι κῦμα (11.307; τρόφι, old word of uncertain sense) | "swollen" (πολλὸν τρόφι "greatly swollen") | "greatly swollen" (+ note: sense uncertain) | "thickly", "in a mass", "in a heap", "curling" |
| πολυπλάγκτοιο ἰωῆς (11.308) | "of the much-straying … blast" | "of the far-roaming wind … rush" | follows the table’s πολύπλαγκτος (17.425) "much-straying" / "far-roaming"; ἰωή "blast, rush" is new |
| ὣς ἄρα πυκνὰ καρήαθ’ ὑφ’ Ἕκτορι δάμνατο λαῶν (11.309) | "so then thick the heads under Hector were overcome, of the people" | "So thick and fast the heads of the people were overcome beneath Hector" | "fell", "were cut down", "were laid low" (each says how); δάμνημι "overcome" per the table’s δαμνάω "overcame" |
| κέκλετ’ Ὀδυσσεύς (11.312) | "called Odysseus" | "if Odysseus had not called on Diomedes" | "gave orders to" (the table’s `i` for κέκλετο): a departure, because Odysseus is not in command of Diomedes and the verb here is an appeal between equals; `l` keeps "called out to" |
| τί παθόντε λελάσμεθα θούριδος ἀλκῆς; (11.313) | "what having suffered, we two, have we forgotten impetuous might?" | "what has come over the two of us, that we have forgotten impetuous might?" | "what is wrong with us", "why have we forgotten", "have we lost our courage"; the dual participle is kept as "the two of us" |
| ἦδος (μίνυνθα ἡμέων ἔσσεται ἦδος, 11.317–318) | "for a short time of us there will be enjoyment" | "the pleasure of having us will be short" (+ note: exact sense uncertain) | "profit", "use", "joy of us"; ἦδος "pleasure" |
| ἀπέπαυσαν πολέμου (11.323) | "from war they had made them cease" | "had put an end to their fighting" | "killed" (the Greek is the euphemism), "disarmed", "stopped them from war"; ἀποπαύω "make cease" |
| κυδοίμεον (11.324) | "were making uproar" | "went … making an uproar of battle" | "were wreaking havoc", "were making confusion", "were raging"; κυδοιμός "din of battle" |
| ἀσπασίως φεύγοντες ἀνέπνεον Ἕκτορα δῖον (11.326–327) | "gladly fleeing, breathed again from heavenly Hector" | "fleeing from heavenly Hector, drew breath again with joy" | "fleeing gladly", "glad of the respite from", "were glad to flee"; ἀσπασίως "gladly" / "with joy" per the table, ἀναπνέω "draw breath again", δῖος "heavenly" |
